Research & Engineering Lineage

SSS-L3 — Software Product Line Engineering

Current scientific findings

Product line engineering asks when coordinated commonality and variability are justified for an actual population of products. The current account separates model validity, real derivation, product acceptance, support and family economics.

This is the current derived account of the separately qualified scientific subject. The full scientific account and four-unit family guide provide its complete reasoning, source qualifications and detailed records. Earlier disclosure labels in the retained historical account below describe its earlier publication cutoff.

A warranted product family

Product Line Engineering begins with an intended population of related products and stakeholders. The question is whether commonality, variability and coordinated production or maintenance yield a justified advantage for that population. A collection of branches, a feature tree or a generator is not sufficient evidence of a useful family. The account distinguishes the family, its models, shared assets, derived products and the organisation or ecosystem that sustains them. Each has a different predicate. A satisfiable feature assignment can be wrong for the stakeholder need; a valid model can be incorrectly realised; a correctly derived product can still fail its acceptance criterion. Accepted report, native property ledger.

The family boundary therefore needs real products or intended products, useful commonality and variation, and an economic or assurance reason to coordinate them. Scope and admission decisions should follow actual consumers and obligations. A small configuration file, selective reuse or deliberate traceable clone-and-own can be adequate. A full platform is not automatically better because it represents more variability. This conditional family warrant prevents the lineage from becoming a universal productisation programme.

Models, binding and actual derivation

Feature models require an explicit interpretation and a supported language. A SAT result establishes satisfaction of the encoded constraints, not adequacy of those constraints or behavior of a generated artifact. Richer model languages and later binding times can add expressiveness while increasing analysis, configuration and operational burdens. There is no universal one-feature/one-module mapping. A feature can crosscut implementation structure; one asset can support several feature combinations; noncode assets can affect the realised product. 62-property source reader.

Derivation needs the actual configuration, assets, tool versions and baseline identities relevant to the promised result. Reusing a generator label does not establish identical inputs or output. Reproducibility asks whether the stipulated derivation relation holds; correctness asks whether the realised product satisfies its criterion. A product can reproduce the same defect perfectly. Conversely, a changed artifact may be equivalent under the intended observer even when byte identity differs. The demanded equivalence should match the purpose rather than silently switch between bytes, structure and behavior.

Assurance and the limits of coverage

Shared assurance transfers only when its premises cover the actual product, assets, configuration and environment. A family-level result can leave residual product checks. A valid selected assignment is not proof that a generator produced that assignment, nor proof that the product's observable behavior is acceptable. The current qualification keeps these stages separate so that a failure in one stage does not falsely refute a true result at another. Accepted property requalification.

Sampling is a finite resource choice under a declared risk and coverage rationale. Pairwise coverage can miss a consequential three-way combination; the tiny 111 discriminator shows the logical gap. Its force is that local coverage does not guarantee a particular untested joint behavior. It does not require exhaustive testing of every possible product in every setting. A known critical triple can be added, a small space can be exhaustively checked, the supported domain can be restricted, or a different adequate realization can remove the fault. The response should be justified by the consequence and premises, not by a universal coverage slogan.

Criticism, composition and novelty

The current record retains 23 critical analyses, ten tensions, 62 ceremony analyses, 53 typed relations, six configurations, nine domain models, eleven inherited cases and six new finite controls. These are different evidence populations, not independent empirical replications. There is no new property identity. Composition model, property ledger with criticism and tensions.

The rejected or unsupported universal forms include a fixed break-even count, a complete up-front platform, feature-tree or SAT validity as sufficient product correctness, pairwise testing as universal assurance, universally late binding, one feature per module, automation as the definition, clones as always inadmissible, names as compatibility evidence, counts as benefits, and model permission as action authority. Their rejection leaves room for the corresponding bounded mechanism where its premises hold. The current account is more useful because it identifies when a smaller mechanism, restricted scope, adequate current baseline or no change can win.

Costs, governance and legitimate alternatives

Automation is a mechanism, not the definition of a product line. AI-generated candidates still need the relevant model, realization and product evidence. ESPLE-048's claim that regeneration is superior over a maintained lifecycle remains unresolved. A promising prototype or successful regeneration does not answer multi-release comprehension, regression, support, cost or governance questions. Conventional generation, maintained assets and bounded assistance remain valid comparators; the unresolved claim does not establish a universal human-only constraint.

Read the complete structured scientific records, exact source and review qualifications, and preliminary existing-owner receiving questions. Finite examples and scientific qualification establish neither deployed effectiveness nor native implementation.

The following original account is retained as dated history. Its property text, evidence and original limitations remain unchanged. Statements that current interpretation was withheld or pending describe the earlier publication boundary; the current account above supplies the new scientific reading route.

This account explains the historical public 62-property study. Its selected sources, limits and analytical conclusions remain at that historical scope. The accepted current r1 interpretation has a separate exact identity and remains subject to source-specific disclosure. Family · Genealogy · All 62 historical properties · Current programme.

When a family is warranted

Software Product Line Engineering studies related products developed through managed commonality and variability, reusable assets and a defined derivation approach. It is more than feature flags, a roadmap or an instruction to share every piece of code. The relevant commitment needs intended products and consumers, useful commonality and variation, and a reason why coordinated production or support is preferable to alternatives. Independent products, selective reuse and traceable clones can remain adequate. Historical public intake.

The historical branches include component reuse, program families, domain analysis, feature modelling, industrial production, implementation techniques and verification. FODA includes domain analysis and rationale beyond a feature diagram. Industrial accounts connect core assets, products and management. Domain and application responsibilities feed back into one another. Proactive, reactive and extractive adoption routes are alternatives, not a universal cost ranking. Historical source table.

Models, realization and product evidence

A feature model needs meaningful semantics. Satisfiability establishes something about the encoded constraints; it cannot reveal every omitted domain obligation or prove that the generator correctly realises the selected product. A successful build is not product correctness. Shared assurance needs an applicable product/configuration/baseline boundary and residual product evidence. More possible configurations do not mean more useful products. Historical property ledger.

Derivation connects a selection to actual assets and a realised member, including noncode dependencies where relevant. A fixed configuration still admits ordinary runtime input and environment variation. A nominal common core does not give an organisation authority over independent participants. Model, product, organisational and operational claims therefore keep different bearers and criteria. Historical public intake, strongest boundaries.

Product failures can reveal missing family knowledge, and a shared repair can be interrupted by a failing variant. Old baselines can remain supported while successors develop. Runtime variation adds obligations over the path between configurations. A formal supervisory model has its own assumptions and reachability properties; it is not certification of a physical deployment. Earlier binding or a fixed arrangement can be simpler when it meets the real need. Historical composition model.

Assurance and economical alternatives

Pairwise testing does not exclude every higher-order fault. Sampling, family analysis, mutation evidence and product testing provide different bounded evidence. Many failing configurations can share one fault, so the number of failures is not the number of independent mechanisms. The family assurance claim must preserve its configuration language, scope, oracle and implementation assumptions. Historical public intake, criticism and evidence.

Comprehensive up-front investment is not always warranted. Product-focused and incremental approaches, selective reuse and the observed use of cloning challenge that universal requirement. A small task experiment cannot price a whole adoption programme, and a successful industrial case is not a universal break-even law. Setup, maintenance, coordination, uncertainty and support horizon determine which alternative is viable. The smallest coherent form can use ordinary modules, a decision table, versioned configuration and a reliable manual procedure. Historical intake and composition.

Criticism and research boundaries

The historical denominator is 62 examined candidates: 49 retained or conditionally useful, 12 non-retained generalisations or ceremonies, and one unresolved replacement hypothesis. The stronger lifecycle claim for regeneration remains unresolved. This does not erase useful bounded assistance or conventional generation. Formal, industrial, qualitative and benchmark evidence retains its actual scope; several works were accessed only through excerpts, abstracts or metadata. All historical records · Exact source table.

The historical research cutoff is 6 September 2026. Its statements about then-announced events remain historical statements; this package does not update or promote them to completed-event evidence. Nor does the public historical source table incorporate private later bibliographic corrections. Readers seeking the current qualified subject should use the exact metadata and the explicit disclosure boundary rather than assume unchanged counts mean unchanged interpretation. Current identity registry.

Existing receiving responsibility

The already-public R003B qualification binds all 62 original members to separate bounded target actions. Its selected actual configuration consumer is the existing package contract and release tooling; it does not claim a new general feature-family architecture, host activation or acceptance of the entire SSS synthesis. The rough Product Line outline preserves #226 and its existing shared owners.

Original form:

Program-family reasoning and enterprise-scoped domain engineering, rather than a claim that any code similarity defines a family.

Problem it addressed:

Superficially similar products can require incompatible assumptions, release obligations or ownership arrangements.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Superficially similar products can require incompatible assumptions, release obligations or ownership arrangements.

Mechanism:

State which products and foreseeable needs belong together; test shared domain assumptions against counterexamples before committing to shared production.

Trigger or context:

A decision to coordinate assets or future variants across more than one product need.

Non trigger or cheap path:

For incidental shared utilities, use ordinary component reuse or independent products without introducing a family programme.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Product needs, differences, expected future use and who can sustain shared assets.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Commonality must survive comparison of actual needs; variation includes intended alternatives, not every historical difference.

Feature semantics and constraints

Features are statements about product needs before they become selectable variables; scope precedes formal completeness.

Variation point and binding time

No binding time is prescribed by scoping; the cost and feasibility of possible binding choices constrain what the family can promise.

Core asset and product relation

Only assets with a defensible cross-product consumer belong in the shared investment case.

Derivation and configuration identity

Scope identifies which derived products the family claims to support; precise baseline identity is established by the production model.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Broader scope can add interactions; scoping alone supplies no coverage or correctness result.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed demand or incompatible product assumptions can require a split, migration or end of shared production.

Ownership and product exception policy

Affected product stakeholders must be represented; legitimate exceptions can invalidate a too-broad common-core assumption.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Expected reuse, coordination and support cost must be compared with independent products or selective component reuse.

ESPLE-003 — Value-bound admission of variability

Formulation

Product-focused scoping and managed variability restrict investment to anticipated family needs.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Product-focused scoping and managed variability restrict investment to anticipated family needs.

Problem it addressed:

Every possible option adds interactions and maintenance without necessarily serving a product.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Every possible option adds interactions and maintenance without necessarily serving a product.

Mechanism:

Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.

Trigger or context:

A request to broaden the set of products or selectable behaviours.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Keep a one-off requirement product-local, or postpone its generalisation until repeated demand supplies evidence.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Demand rationale, expected reuse, interaction impact and costs of both local and shared realisation.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Commonality must survive comparison of actual needs; variation includes intended alternatives, not every historical difference.

Feature semantics and constraints

Features are statements about product needs before they become selectable variables; scope precedes formal completeness.

Variation point and binding time

No binding time is prescribed by scoping; the cost and feasibility of possible binding choices constrain what the family can promise.

Core asset and product relation

Only assets with a defensible cross-product consumer belong in the shared investment case.

Derivation and configuration identity

Scope identifies which derived products the family claims to support; precise baseline identity is established by the production model.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Broader scope can add interactions; scoping alone supplies no coverage or correctness result.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed demand or incompatible product assumptions can require a split, migration or end of shared production.

Ownership and product exception policy

Affected product stakeholders must be represented; legitimate exceptions can invalidate a too-broad common-core assumption.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Expected reuse, coordination and support cost must be compared with independent products or selective component reuse.

An admitted option has a consumer and support path; rejected or deferred options retain their rationale.

Keep a one-off requirement product-local, or postpone its generalisation until repeated demand supplies evidence.

Support and retirement

Reassess the option when its demand disappears; support-aware removal is a separate obligation in ESPLE-061.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Every possible option adds interactions and maintenance without necessarily serving a product. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product sponsors and shared-asset maintainers negotiate the scope; this criterion does not require a new board for each feature.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product sponsors and shared-asset maintainers negotiate the scope; this criterion does not require a new board for each feature. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Demand rationale, expected reuse, interaction impact and costs of both local and shared realisation.; the result must expose An admitted option has a consumer and support path; rejected or deferred options retain their rationale. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

An admitted option has a consumer and support path; rejected or deferred options retain their rationale.

Known failure modes:

  • Overly restrictive admission can suppress valuable experimentation; speculative demand can also be used to justify permanent complexity.

  • Decision latency and potential lost opportunities from deferral.

ESPLE-004 — Coupled domain and application responsibilities

FAST and major SPLE frameworks distinguish domain assets from application derivation while coupling their work.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

FAST and major SPLE frameworks distinguish domain assets from application derivation while coupling their work.

Problem it addressed:

A reusable platform can become detached from products, or product teams can silently duplicate domain responsibility.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A reusable platform can become detached from products, or product teams can silently duplicate domain responsibility.

Mechanism:

Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.

Trigger or context:

At least one asset or production decision is intended to serve several products.

Non trigger or cheap path:

The same people may perform both activities; a small family needs no separate departments or serial phases.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Defined family scope, asset responsibilities and actual product requests.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.

Commonality and variability assumptions

The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.

Feature semantics and constraints

Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.

Variation point and binding time

Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.

Core asset and product relation

Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.

Evolution and migration obligations

Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.

Ownership and product exception policy

The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P2

Property specific application
Family

P2

Trigger

At least one asset or production decision is intended to serve several products.

Consequential inputs

Defined family scope, asset responsibilities and actual product requests.

Realisation or decision

Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.

Acceptance boundary

Product work can identify the reusable baseline it consumes, and asset work can identify the products it supports.

Non family or cheaper alternative

The same people may perform both activities; a small family needs no separate departments or serial phases.

Support and retirement

If no cross-product asset remains, use a single-product process rather than preserve two ceremonial tracks.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A reusable platform can become detached from products, or product teams can silently duplicate domain responsibility. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Asset developers and product developers need reciprocal access to decisions; management supplies resources rather than treating a model as authority.

Actor and authority boundary:

Asset developers and product developers need reciprocal access to decisions; management supplies resources rather than treating a model as authority. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Defined family scope, asset responsibilities and actual product requests.; the result must expose Product work can identify the reusable baseline it consumes, and asset work can identify the products it supports. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Product work can identify the reusable baseline it consumes, and asset work can identify the products it supports.

Known failure modes:

  • Organisational separation can become a bottleneck or produce assets nobody uses. The distinction is about responsibilities, not a mandatory team topology.

  • Coordination and reconciliation of competing release schedules.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Organisational separation can become a bottleneck or produce assets nobody uses. The distinction is about responsibilities, not a mandatory team topology.

Original form:

Application experience feeds domain requirements, assets and production processes in iterative product-line frameworks.

Problem it addressed:

Defects, workarounds and new needs stay local while the shared platform continues producing the same mismatch.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Defects, workarounds and new needs stay local while the shared platform continues producing the same mismatch.

Mechanism:

Return a product observation with its configuration, asset baseline and consequence; decide whether to repair the core, adjust a constraint, retain an exception or revise scope.

Trigger or context:

Derivation failure, recurring local workaround, unexpected interaction or a justified new common need.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A direct conversation and linked change record can suffice when the team and affected products are small.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Reproducible observation, affected product context and a maintainer able to change the relevant shared asset.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.

Commonality and variability assumptions

The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.

Feature semantics and constraints

Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.

Variation point and binding time

Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.

Core asset and product relation

Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.

Evolution and migration obligations

Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.

Ownership and product exception policy

The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

Family

Original form:

Extractive/reactive adoption and industrial mixed-platform practice allow product-specific differences rather than requiring one universal core.

Problem it addressed:

Either all exceptions are forbidden, or local forks erase the relationship needed for fixes and future extraction.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Either all exceptions are forbidden, or local forks erase the relationship needed for fixes and future extraction.

Mechanism:

Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.

Trigger or context:

A product obligation cannot be met adequately through the current shared assets without disproportionate disruption.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A small isolated patch with a recorded origin may be better than a new family-wide variation point.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Product obligation, impact on other products and an owner willing to maintain the exception.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.

Commonality and variability assumptions

The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.

Feature semantics and constraints

Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.

Variation point and binding time

Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.

Core asset and product relation

Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.

Evolution and migration obligations

Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.

Ownership and product exception policy

The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

A compulsory large upfront platform investment can outrun demand or discard working products.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A compulsory large upfront platform investment can outrun demand or discard working products.

Mechanism:

Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.

Trigger or context:

Starting a product line or changing how an existing portfolio is produced.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Reuse a few stable assets or retain clone-and-own while collecting evidence; no immediate platform conversion is required.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Demand horizon, asset state, change rate, budget and the cost of delaying products.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.

Commonality and variability assumptions

The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.

Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.

Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.

Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.

Evolution and migration obligations

Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.

Ownership and product exception policy

The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A compulsory large upfront platform investment can outrun demand or discard working products. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Actor and authority boundary:

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The chosen route states what is invested now, what remains product-local and what evidence triggers further consolidation.

Known failure modes:

  • Reactive growth can accumulate hidden debt, extraction can preserve accidental variation, and proactive design can overfit forecasts.

  • Each route distributes investment, interruption and future rework differently.

ESPLE-008 — Explicit feature semantics

Historical source pointer: /properties/7 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Feature modelling organises domain-relevant characteristics, but implementation variables and stakeholder features need not coincide.

  • ESPLE-S009

  • ESPLE-S014

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Esple-s005

1990-11

Esple-s009

2005

Esple-s014

2005

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Feature modelling organises domain-relevant characteristics, but implementation variables and stakeholder features need not coincide.

Problem it addressed:

The same word is treated as a requirement, a module and a selectable flag despite different meanings.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

The same word is treated as a requirement, a module and a selectable flag despite different meanings.

Mechanism:

Define what each feature denotes, who interprets it and how selections relate to requirements, implementation and runtime capability.

Trigger or context:

Features are used to negotiate products, derive artefacts or justify assurance.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A compact glossary plus explicit configuration rules can be sufficient; a tree is optional.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Stakeholder vocabulary, variation decisions and the relevant implementation mapping.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common and variable characteristics are explicit semantic decisions; historical product observations do not exhaust valid possibilities.

Feature semantics and constraints

Boolean, cardinality, attribute and typed constraints describe encoded validity; domain adequacy must be checked outside solver consistency.

Variation point and binding time

A model choice may bind before build, at deployment or at runtime; selection semantics do not determine realisation timing by themselves.

Core asset and product relation

Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.

Derivation and configuration identity

A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.

Ownership and product exception policy

Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P3

Property specific application
Family

P3

Trigger

Features are used to negotiate products, derive artefacts or justify assurance.

Consequential inputs

Stakeholder vocabulary, variation decisions and the relevant implementation mapping.

Realisation or decision

Define what each feature denotes, who interprets it and how selections relate to requirements, implementation and runtime capability.

Acceptance boundary

A selected feature has a checkable meaning at the product boundary, including attributes or multiplicity where required.

Non family or cheaper alternative

A compact glossary plus explicit configuration rules can be sufficient; a tree is optional.

Support and retirement

Remove semantic entries only with the associated supported feature or replace them with an explicit migration mapping.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: The same word is treated as a requirement, a module and a selectable flag despite different meanings. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Domain experts, configurators and developers must resolve semantic disagreement; the modeller cannot decide stakeholder intent by naming a node.

Actor and authority boundary:

Domain experts, configurators and developers must resolve semantic disagreement; the modeller cannot decide stakeholder intent by naming a node. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Stakeholder vocabulary, variation decisions and the relevant implementation mapping.; the result must expose A selected feature has a checkable meaning at the product boundary, including attributes or multiplicity where required. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A selected feature has a checkable meaning at the product boundary, including attributes or multiplicity where required.

Known failure modes:

  • Excessive semantic formalisation can overwhelm users; unqualified shared names conceal version or domain differences.

  • Definition, explanation and coordinated updates across representations.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Excessive semantic formalisation can overwhelm users; unqualified shared names conceal version or domain differences.

Original form:

Propositional interpretations enable detection of void models, dead features and unintentionally forced options.

Problem it addressed:

Encoded constraints contradict one another or make purported choices impossible.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Encoded constraints contradict one another or make purported choices impossible.

Mechanism:

Check the model's declared semantics for consistency and investigate diagnoses relative to intended configurations; report the exact model and solver interpretation.

Trigger or context:

Constraints are nontrivial, edited, combined or used to reject user selections.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Exhaustive enumeration or a manually checked decision table may suffice for a tiny model.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A defined constraint language, faithful encoding and intended interpretations for anomalies.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common and variable characteristics are explicit semantic decisions; historical product observations do not exhaust valid possibilities.

Feature semantics and constraints

Boolean, cardinality, attribute and typed constraints describe encoded validity; domain adequacy must be checked outside solver consistency.

Variation point and binding time

A model choice may bind before build, at deployment or at runtime; selection semantics do not determine realisation timing by themselves.

Core asset and product relation

Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.

Derivation and configuration identity

A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.

Ownership and product exception policy

Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

The checked model has a satisfiable witness or an understood inconsistency; apparent anomalies have domain dispositions.

Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.

A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.

Ownership and product exception policy

Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

Formulation

Configuration analysis and human-oriented extraction produce explanations and comprehensible constraints, not merely yes/no answers.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Configuration analysis and human-oriented extraction produce explanations and comprehensible constraints, not merely yes/no answers.

Problem it addressed:

Users cannot repair a rejected configuration or understand why an option disappeared.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Users cannot repair a rejected configuration or understand why an option disappeared.

Mechanism:

Relate a conflict or forced choice to the smallest useful set of decisions and constraints; permit human correction and show relevant provenance.

Trigger or context:

Configuration choices are numerous, cross-constrained or made by users without implementation expertise.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A domain expert can explain a small stable set of rules directly; automated minimal explanations are not always needed.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Meaningful feature semantics, decision history and a link from the diagnosis to a possible user action.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common and variable characteristics are explicit semantic decisions; historical product observations do not exhaust valid possibilities.

Feature semantics and constraints

Boolean, cardinality, attribute and typed constraints describe encoded validity; domain adequacy must be checked outside solver consistency.

Variation point and binding time

A model choice may bind before build, at deployment or at runtime; selection semantics do not determine realisation timing by themselves.

Core asset and product relation

Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.

Derivation and configuration identity

A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.

Ownership and product exception policy

Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

Property specific application
Family

Trigger

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Users cannot repair a rejected configuration or understand why an option disappeared. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Actor and authority boundary:

Configurators and domain experts; an explanation assists choice but must not conceal alternative repairs or silently change requirements. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Meaningful feature semantics, decision history and a link from the diagnosis to a possible user action.; the result must expose The consumer can identify an acceptable repair or understand why no permitted product meets the request. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The consumer can identify an acceptable repair or understand why no permitted product meets the request.

Known failure modes:

  • Logical minimality need not yield human usefulness. Simplified formulas may obscure their relation to implementation evidence.

  • Explanation generation, interface maintenance and validation with users.

Logical minimality need not yield human usefulness. Simplified formulas may obscure their relation to implementation evidence.

ESPLE-013 — Deliberate binding-time selection

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Variability may be resolved during development, compilation, deployment or execution; binding time changes the engineering problem.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S030

Esple-s017

2009

Esple-s030

2008

2005

Esple-s043

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Variability may be resolved during development, compilation, deployment or execution; binding time changes the engineering problem.

Problem it addressed:

Postponing selection retains flexibility but may also retain code, configuration hazards and transition obligations.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Postponing selection retains flexibility but may also retain code, configuration hazards and transition obligations.

Mechanism:

Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.

Trigger or context:

A variation point is introduced or its resolution time changes.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Bind early when the required choice is already known and later change has no justified value.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Timing of product knowledge, resource limits, supported changes and operational safety constraints.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Shared code, product-specific code and interaction glue may coexist; arbitrary duplication is neither automatically valuable nor forbidden.

Feature semantics and constraints

Selection-to-implementation relations must preserve feature meaning; syntactic modularity alone does not establish semantic alignment.

Variation point and binding time

Compile, deployment and runtime binding carry different footprint, timing and transition obligations; later is not universally better.

Core asset and product relation

Assets may be annotated, composed, parameterised or transformed; the core need not be one monolithic source tree.

Derivation and configuration identity

Generator, template, build and dependency versions can affect the realised variant and belong in relevant provenance.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Cross-mechanism interactions require checks; successful code generation or compilation is not product correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changes to realisation or binding time can invalidate mappings, supported configurations and previous assurance.

Ownership and product exception policy

Implementers choose within family obligations; product-local exceptions require explicit support and do not inherit all shared claims.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Technique complexity must be earned by demand and assurance needs; ordinary parameters, modules or manual derivation remain alternatives.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P4

Property specific application
Family

P4

Trigger

A variation point is introduced or its resolution time changes.

Consequential inputs

Timing of product knowledge, resource limits, supported changes and operational safety constraints.

Realisation or decision

Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.

Acceptance boundary

The implementation resolves the choice at the declared point, and the corresponding invariants and failure handling have been checked.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Bind early when the required choice is already known and later change has no justified value.

Support and retirement

Remove late-binding infrastructure when the need to change at runtime disappears; do not remove support for existing variants silently.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Postponing selection retains flexibility but may also retain code, configuration hazards and transition obligations. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product architects, build/deployment engineers and operators where relevant; runtime rebinding needs actual operational permission.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product architects, build/deployment engineers and operators where relevant; runtime rebinding needs actual operational permission. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Timing of product knowledge, resource limits, supported changes and operational safety constraints.; the result must expose The implementation resolves the choice at the declared point, and the corresponding invariants and failure handling have been checked. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The implementation resolves the choice at the declared point, and the corresponding invariants and failure handling have been checked.

Known failure modes:

  • Early binding can multiply builds and reduce responsiveness; late binding can multiply reachable states and prevent removal of unwanted functionality.

  • Build diversity, deployment coordination or runtime complexity, depending on the chosen time.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Early binding can multiply builds and reduce responsiveness; late binding can multiply reachable states and prevent removal of unwanted functionality.

Consequential changes or product construction depend on understanding how a feature is realised.

Local naming, module structure and a small checked mapping can replace a comprehensive trace database.

Feature semantics, actual artefacts and the consumers of impact or derivation information.

Family scope and expected reuse

Changes to realisation or binding time can invalidate mappings, supported configurations and previous assurance.

Ownership and product exception policy

Implementers choose within family obligations; product-local exceptions require explicit support and do not inherit all shared claims.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Technique complexity must be earned by demand and assurance needs; ordinary parameters, modules or manual derivation remain alternatives.

Delta-oriented programming derives variants by conditionally applying ordered modifications to a base.

Esple-s018

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Delta-oriented programming derives variants by conditionally applying ordered modifications to a base.

Problem it addressed:

Purely additive feature composition struggles with variants requiring removal or replacement of existing behaviour.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Purely additive feature composition struggles with variants requiring removal or replacement of existing behaviour.

Mechanism:

Define applicable deltas, their dependencies or order and the validity conditions of each modification; verify the resulting product rather than assuming arbitrary edits commute.

Trigger or context:

Product differences naturally require structured additions, removals or changes over a shared base.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use direct modules or parameters where no meaningful transformation sequence is needed.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A base program, delta applicability conditions, ordering constraints and language-specific well-formedness checks.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Shared code, product-specific code and interaction glue may coexist; arbitrary duplication is neither automatically valuable nor forbidden.

Feature semantics and constraints

Selection-to-implementation relations must preserve feature meaning; syntactic modularity alone does not establish semantic alignment.

Variation point and binding time

Compile, deployment and runtime binding carry different footprint, timing and transition obligations; later is not universally better.

Core asset and product relation

Assets may be annotated, composed, parameterised or transformed; the core need not be one monolithic source tree.

Derivation and configuration identity

Generator, template, build and dependency versions can affect the realised variant and belong in relevant provenance.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Cross-mechanism interactions require checks; successful code generation or compilation is not product correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changes to realisation or binding time can invalidate mappings, supported configurations and previous assurance.

Ownership and product exception policy

Implementers choose within family obligations; product-local exceptions require explicit support and do not inherit all shared claims.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Technique complexity must be earned by demand and assurance needs; ordinary parameters, modules or manual derivation remain alternatives.

Family

Product differences naturally require structured additions, removals or changes over a shared base.

Each selected delta is applicable in its context and the ordered derivation yields a well-formed product meeting selected requirements.

Support and retirement

Replace deltas with a simpler representation when the transformation structure no longer provides useful reuse or separation.

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Purely additive feature composition struggles with variants requiring removal or replacement of existing behaviour. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Product-line implementers and type/consistency analysers; a delta is a proposed construction step, not unrestricted authority to modify any supported product.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product-line implementers and type/consistency analysers; a delta is a proposed construction step, not unrestricted authority to modify any supported product. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: A base program, delta applicability conditions, ordering constraints and language-specific well-formedness checks.; the result must expose Each selected delta is applicable in its context and the ordered derivation yields a well-formed product meeting selected requirements. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Each selected delta is applicable in its context and the ordered derivation yields a well-formed product meeting selected requirements.

  • Additional representation, applicability checks and maintenance of transformations as the base evolves.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Core assets include requirements, architecture, tests, documentation, tools and production knowledge, not only reusable code.

Problem it addressed:

Code is shared but every product must rediscover its requirements, test basis or construction instructions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Code is shared but every product must rediscover its requirements, test basis or construction instructions.

Mechanism:

Treat non-code work products as reusable assets where products actually consume them, with compatible versioning and variation information.

Trigger or context:

Repeated product work depends on shared engineering knowledge beyond implementation code.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Share only the few requirements, tests or instructions that have a real consumer; a full document suite is not obligatory.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Identified product consumers, scope of reuse and responsibility for keeping the asset valid.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.

Feature semantics and constraints

A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.

Variation point and binding time

Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.

Core asset and product relation

Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.

Ownership and product exception policy

Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

Original form:

A production plan explains how core assets are used to build products, including roles, inputs, sequence and tool compatibility.

Problem it addressed:

The family repository exists, but product production depends on undocumented personal knowledge.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

The family repository exists, but product production depends on undocumented personal knowledge.

Mechanism:

Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.

Trigger or context:

Products must be reproduced, handed to another team or built repeatedly from shared assets.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A short script plus explicit human decisions can be a complete plan for a small stable family.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Asset catalogue, configuration decisions, compatible tool versions and product acceptance criteria.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.

Feature semantics and constraints

A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.

Variation point and binding time

Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.

Core asset and product relation

Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.

Ownership and product exception policy

Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

Family

Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.

Acceptance boundary

A competent builder can derive the intended product from declared inputs and identify unsupported deviations.

Non family or cheaper alternative

A short script plus explicit human decisions can be a complete plan for a small stable family.

Support and retirement

Delete unused steps and retire plans for unsupported baselines; retain what is needed to reproduce obligations still in force.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: The family repository exists, but product production depends on undocumented personal knowledge. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product builders execute the plan and return obstacles to maintainers; the plan does not itself accept a release.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product builders execute the plan and return obstacles to maintainers; the plan does not itself accept a release. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Asset catalogue, configuration decisions, compatible tool versions and product acceptance criteria.; the result must expose A competent builder can derive the intended product from declared inputs and identify unsupported deviations. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A competent builder can derive the intended product from declared inputs and identify unsupported deviations.

Known failure modes:

  • A plan can lag the actual process or prescribe steps with no useful output. Full automation may be costly without sufficient volume.

  • Keeping instructions and executable production infrastructure consistent.

Property specific objection

A plan can lag the actual process or prescribe steps with no useful output. Full automation may be costly without sufficient volume.

Starting form

A production plan explains how core assets are used to build products, including roles, inputs, sequence and tool compatibility.

Criticism and change

A plan can lag the actual process or prescribe steps with no useful output. Full automation may be costly without sufficient volume. Mature response: Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.

Supported transitions

    ESPLE-C22

    Class

    REFINED

    Judgement

    Retain production control, not maximal documentation or universal byte-for-byte build identity. This is a synthesis of distinct evidence, not a reported comparative trial of provenance policies.

Caution

These are sourced branch developments plus explicitly analytical refinements; they are not a claim of one linear historical progression.

Mature or evolved form:

Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.

Ceremony vs property:

Ledger id

ESPLE-CS020

Minimal adequate alternative

A short script plus explicit human decisions can be a complete plan for a small stable family.

Retirement condition

Delete unused steps and retire plans for unsupported baselines; retain what is needed to reproduce obligations still in force.

Cost

Keeping instructions and executable production infrastructure consistent.

ESPLE-021 — Configuration, asset and tool baseline identity

Historical source pointer: /properties/20 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Production planning links products to versions of assets, tools and configuration decisions.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S011

  • ESPLE-S021

  • ESPLE-S041

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s011

2002-06

Esple-s021

2018 online; 2019 journal

Esple-s041

2018 conference; 2021-10-12 arXiv deposit

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Production planning links products to versions of assets, tools and configuration decisions.

Problem it addressed:

A defect or result cannot be associated with the exact variant and baseline that produced it.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A defect or result cannot be associated with the exact variant and baseline that produced it.

Mechanism:

Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.

Trigger or context:

Reproduction, support, change impact or transfer of an assurance result depends on knowing what was built.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A versioned configuration file and pinned build inputs may suffice; a new provenance service is not inherently required.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Actual build inputs and the equivalence level required for support or assurance.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.

Feature semantics and constraints

A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.

Variation point and binding time

Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.

Core asset and product relation

Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.

Ownership and product exception policy

Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P5

Property specific application
Family

P5

Trigger

Reproduction, support, change impact or transfer of an assurance result depends on knowing what was built.

Consequential inputs

Actual build inputs and the equivalence level required for support or assurance.

Realisation or decision

Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.

Acceptance boundary

A reported product can be traced to its actual derivation inputs and distinguished from a similarly named but different baseline.

Non family or cheaper alternative

A versioned configuration file and pinned build inputs may suffice; a new provenance service is not inherently required.

Support and retirement

Reduce retention when support and reproducibility obligations end, not merely because the current mainline has moved on.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A defect or result cannot be associated with the exact variant and baseline that produced it. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Builders, maintainers and acceptance reviewers exchange product identities; an identifier is evidence of naming, not proof of semantic correctness.

Actor and authority boundary:

Builders, maintainers and acceptance reviewers exchange product identities; an identifier is evidence of naming, not proof of semantic correctness. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Actual build inputs and the equivalence level required for support or assurance.; the result must expose A reported product can be traced to its actual derivation inputs and distinguished from a similarly named but different baseline. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A reported product can be traced to its actual derivation inputs and distinguished from a similarly named but different baseline.

Known failure modes:

  • Incomplete capture of dependencies or generated inputs makes provenance misleading; exact hashes do not explain feature semantics.

  • Recording and retaining relevant inputs and resolving external dependency changes.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Incomplete capture of dependencies or generated inputs makes provenance misleading; exact hashes do not explain feature semantics.

Original form:

Defined derivation makes repeatable product construction possible; exact binary reproducibility is a stronger, separate condition.

Problem it addressed:

Repeating the apparent same derivation silently produces a materially different product.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Repeating the apparent same derivation silently produces a materially different product.

Mechanism:

Declare whether repeatability means equal feature realisation, equivalent tested behaviour, identical generated source or identical bytes, then control the inputs necessary for that claim.

Trigger or context:

Support, certification, comparison or distribution requires reliable reconstruction of a product.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Behavioural or structural equivalence may be adequate; do not impose bit-for-bit output where timestamps or tool differences are immaterial.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A declared equivalence criterion, relevant environment inputs and known nondeterministic steps.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.

Feature semantics and constraints

A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.

Variation point and binding time

Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.

Core asset and product relation

Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.

Ownership and product exception policy

Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Relax controls whose stronger identity is no longer consumed, while retaining enough information for supported products.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Repeating the apparent same derivation silently produces a materially different product. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Actor and authority boundary:

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A repeat derivation meets the declared equivalence criterion, or differences are explained and adjudicated.

  • Byte identity can coexist with the same defect; behavioural equivalence can be difficult to establish; environment capture can be expensive.

  • Pinning, isolation, retained infrastructure and comparison effort.

Byte identity can coexist with the same defect; behavioural equivalence can be difficult to establish; environment capture can be expensive.

Lineage class:
