Original form:

Product-line analyses establish different kinds of result over models, code, configurations and behaviour.

Problem it addressed:

Evidence at one layer is promoted into a stronger claim about the entire product family.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Evidence at one layer is promoted into a stronger claim about the entire product family.

Mechanism:

State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.

Trigger or context:

A model, test, proof or analysis result is used to justify a product or family decision.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A concise claim-and-boundary statement attached to the result can be sufficient.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Actual analysis semantics, configuration coverage, tool limitations and product identity.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

Original form:

Feature interactions can create behaviour that no isolated feature analysis reveals.

Problem it addressed:

Products fail only when particular combinations, inputs or environments occur together.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Products fail only when particular combinations, inputs or environments occur together.

Mechanism:

Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.

Trigger or context:

Features share state, resources, protocols, build choices or behavioural assumptions.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Isolated independent substitutions may need only interface checks; do not impose high-order combinatorial testing without an interaction rationale.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Dependency evidence, known faults, changed features and the operational conditions under which they combine.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

Original form:

Sampling reduces the number of configured products analysed, including combinatorial and coverage-oriented strategies.

Problem it addressed:

Exhaustive product testing is too expensive, but an arbitrary sample leaves its omissions unexplained.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Exhaustive product testing is too expensive, but an arbitrary sample leaves its omissions unexplained.

Mechanism:

Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.

Trigger or context:

Full enumeration is infeasible and a bounded sample can provide useful assurance.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Test every supported configuration when the family is small, or analyse a relevant shared property once when a sound family analysis is cheaper.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Configuration constraints, test cost, fault-risk assumptions and a meaningful comparison baseline.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

ESPLE-026 — Family-based sharing of analysis

Historical source pointer: /properties/25 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Family-based analyses share computation over variability rather than enumerate every product separately.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S019

  • ESPLE-S022

  • ESPLE-S040

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Family-based analyses share computation over variability rather than enumerate every product separately.

Problem it addressed:

Repeated analysis duplicates work over common code and cannot scale with the number of configurations.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Repeated analysis duplicates work over common code and cannot scale with the number of configurations.

Mechanism:

Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.

Trigger or context:

Many products share analyzable structure and the analysis implementation supports their variability semantics.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Ordinary product analysis is preferable for a few configurations or unsupported languages and artefacts.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Correct variability-aware representation, configuration constraints and a sound underlying analysis for the claim in question.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P6

Property specific application
Family

P6

Trigger

Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.

Acceptance boundary

Results correspond to the intended per-product analysis across the represented configurations, with conditional warnings and unsupported cases exposed.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Ordinary product analysis is preferable for a few configurations or unsupported languages and artefacts.

Support and retirement

Use a simpler product or compositional approach when sharing no longer offsets infrastructure and analysis costs.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Repeated analysis duplicates work over common code and cannot scale with the number of configurations. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Analysis engineers produce conditional results for developers and reviewers; coverage of configurations is not coverage of every kind of bug.

Actor and authority boundary:

Analysis engineers produce conditional results for developers and reviewers; coverage of configurations is not coverage of every kind of bug. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Correct variability-aware representation, configuration constraints and a sound underlying analysis for the claim in question.; the result must expose Results correspond to the intended per-product analysis across the represented configurations, with conditional warnings and unsupported cases exposed. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Results correspond to the intended per-product analysis across the represented configurations, with conditional warnings and unsupported cases exposed.

  • Specialised infrastructure, memory, model extraction and interpretation of conditional results.

Original form:

Feature-wise and compositional reasoning attempts to combine local results under explicit interfaces and assumptions.

Problem it addressed:

Rechecking every product is costly, but isolated feature correctness may not survive composition.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Rechecking every product is costly, but isolated feature correctness may not survive composition.

Mechanism:

State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.

Trigger or context:

Stable interfaces and separable properties make local reasoning reusable across products.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Check the whole derived product when contracts would be harder to specify or maintain than the verification itself.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Explicit environmental assumptions, composition semantics and evidence that the actual interfaces meet the contracts.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

ESPLE-028 — Acceptance of the actual derived product

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Historical origin:

Formulation

Application engineering tests particular products in addition to reusable domain assets.

  • ESPLE-S009

  • ESPLE-S021

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Esple-s006

2000

Esple-s009

2005

Esple-s021

2018 online; 2019 journal

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Application engineering tests particular products in addition to reusable domain assets.

Problem it addressed:

A product inherits a family label despite a defective build, omitted requirement or product-specific integration problem.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A product inherits a family label despite a defective build, omitted requirement or product-specific integration problem.

Mechanism:

Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.

Trigger or context:

A product is delivered, deployed or materially changed.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Reuse valid existing evidence and perform only the additional product checks needed for unestablished obligations; repeated full testing is not automatically required.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Product identity, selected requirements, environment and applicable family-level results.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P6

Property specific application
Family

P6

Trigger

A product is delivered, deployed or materially changed.

Consequential inputs

Product identity, selected requirements, environment and applicable family-level results.

Realisation or decision

Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.

Acceptance boundary

The accepted product is the one tested or otherwise justified, and unresolved obligations are explicit to the decision-maker.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Reuse valid existing evidence and perform only the additional product checks needed for unestablished obligations; repeated full testing is not automatically required.

Support and retirement

Reuse an unchanged valid result instead of rerunning ceremony; retire acceptance claims when material assumptions change.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A product inherits a family label despite a defective build, omitted requirement or product-specific integration problem. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product acceptance and operational stakeholders decide readiness; core-asset maintainers supply evidence but do not replace local obligations.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product acceptance and operational stakeholders decide readiness; core-asset maintainers supply evidence but do not replace local obligations. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Product identity, selected requirements, environment and applicable family-level results.; the result must expose The accepted product is the one tested or otherwise justified, and unresolved obligations are explicit to the decision-maker. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The accepted product is the one tested or otherwise justified, and unresolved obligations are explicit to the decision-maker.

Known failure modes:

  • Product-only testing can duplicate effort and miss unsampled family defects; acceptance criteria themselves may be incomplete.

  • Builds, tests, domain-specific evidence and coordination of release decisions.

ESPLE-030 — Semantic classification of feature-model edits

Historical source pointer: /properties/29 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Feature-model edit analysis distinguishes changes by their effect on represented configuration sets.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S023

  • ESPLE-S024

  • ESPLE-S039

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s023

2009

Esple-s024

2013 preprint/online; 2014 journal

Esple-s039

2025

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Feature-model edit analysis distinguishes changes by their effect on represented configuration sets.

Problem it addressed:

Syntactically small edits silently add or remove permitted products.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Syntactically small edits silently add or remove permitted products.

Mechanism:

Compare old and new model semantics using an explicit feature correspondence; classify preserved, added and removed configurations before selecting migration or regression work.

Trigger or context:

A feature model, cross-tree constraint or feature vocabulary changes.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Enumerate and compare all configurations for a small family rather than introduce a specialised solver.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Both model versions, feature identity mapping and the intended semantic relation.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P7

Property specific application
Family

P7

Trigger

A feature model, cross-tree constraint or feature vocabulary changes.

Consequential inputs

Both model versions, feature identity mapping and the intended semantic relation.

Realisation or decision

Compare old and new model semantics using an explicit feature correspondence; classify preserved, added and removed configurations before selecting migration or regression work.

Acceptance boundary

The semantic effect is supported by witnesses, counterexamples or a justified equivalence result under the stated mapping.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Enumerate and compare all configurations for a small family rather than introduce a specialised solver.

Support and retirement

Skip a new comparison when no relevant model semantics changed and this is established by an adequate simpler check.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Syntactically small edits silently add or remove permitted products. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Modellers, product maintainers and test planners consume the classification; set preservation does not certify unchanged implementation behaviour.

Actor and authority boundary:

Modellers, product maintainers and test planners consume the classification; set preservation does not certify unchanged implementation behaviour. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Both model versions, feature identity mapping and the intended semantic relation.; the result must expose The semantic effect is supported by witnesses, counterexamples or a justified equivalence result under the stated mapping. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The semantic effect is supported by witnesses, counterexamples or a justified equivalence result under the stated mapping.

Known failure modes:

  • Equal feature names can conceal changed meaning; different feature universes require careful projection; formal comparison cannot recover omitted domain intent.

  • Maintaining correspondence and computing semantic differences.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Equal feature names can conceal changed meaning; different feature universes require careful projection; formal comparison cannot recover omitted domain intent.

ESPLE-031 — Intent-preserving configuration migration

Historical source pointer: /properties/30 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Configuration migration can require sequences of changes, feature-model drift and preservation of supported product obligations.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S011

  • ESPLE-S024

  • ESPLE-S041

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s011

2002-06

Esple-s024

2013 preprint/online; 2014 journal

Esple-s041

2018 conference; 2021-10-12 arXiv deposit

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Configuration migration can require sequences of changes, feature-model drift and preservation of supported product obligations.

Problem it addressed:

An old configuration becomes invalid, or a valid replacement no longer fulfils the product's intended role.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

An old configuration becomes invalid, or a valid replacement no longer fulfils the product's intended role.

Mechanism:

Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.

Trigger or context:

A supported product must move to a changed model, core baseline or production environment.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Retain a supported older baseline or use a reviewed manual migration when the portfolio is small.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Old identity, new constraints, stakeholder intent, supported transition paths and acceptance evidence.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P7

Property specific application
Family

P7

Trigger

A supported product must move to a changed model, core baseline or production environment.

Old identity, new constraints, stakeholder intent, supported transition paths and acceptance evidence.

Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.

Acceptance boundary

The migrated product satisfies the relevant new constraints and preserved obligations, or explicit accepted changes are recorded.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Retain a supported older baseline or use a reviewed manual migration when the portfolio is small.

Support and retirement

End migration machinery for retired baselines only after outstanding support obligations are resolved.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: An old configuration becomes invalid, or a valid replacement no longer fulfils the product's intended role. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product maintainers and stakeholders approve changed selections; a migration optimiser proposes solutions within authorised objectives.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product maintainers and stakeholders approve changed selections; a migration optimiser proposes solutions within authorised objectives. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Old identity, new constraints, stakeholder intent, supported transition paths and acceptance evidence.; the result must expose The migrated product satisfies the relevant new constraints and preserved obligations, or explicit accepted changes are recorded. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The migrated product satisfies the relevant new constraints and preserved obligations, or explicit accepted changes are recorded.

Known failure modes:

  • Minimal feature edits need not minimise labour or preserve meaning; synthetic optimisation performance is not real migration benefit.

  • Migration planning, compatibility work, testing and temporary coexistence of baselines.

Minimal feature edits need not minimise labour or preserve meaning; synthetic optimisation performance is not real migration benefit.

Production plans and industrial families relate product releases to supported core-asset and tool versions.

2013 preprint/online; 2014 journal

2018 conference; 2021-10-12 arXiv deposit

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Production plans and industrial families relate product releases to supported core-asset and tool versions.

Problem it addressed:

Independently released products silently consume incompatible assets or lose maintenance support when the core moves ahead.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Independently released products silently consume incompatible assets or lose maintenance support when the core moves ahead.

Mechanism:

State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.

Trigger or context:

Products, core assets or tools evolve on different schedules.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A single synchronised release may be adequate when all products and stakeholders can genuinely move together.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Compatibility evidence, support commitments and product delivery schedules.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Independently released products silently consume incompatible assets or lose maintenance support when the core moves ahead. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Each supported product has an identifiable maintenance path and compatible production baseline.

Original form:

Evolving feature models can invalidate configuration-oriented test suites; repair, regeneration and change-specific selection are distinct strategies.

Problem it addressed:

Old tests exercise invalid or irrelevant configurations while newly introduced configurations receive no attention.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Old tests exercise invalid or irrelevant configurations while newly introduced configurations receive no attention.

Mechanism:

Reassess test-configuration validity and purpose after model change; choose repair, fresh generation or targeted new-product tests according to regression and novelty objectives.

Trigger or context:

A feature-model change alters permitted products or test-selection assumptions.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Retain still-valid tests and manually add a few relevant configurations when changes are small.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Old tests, old/new model semantics, test costs and the risk of old versus newly admitted configurations.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Acceptance boundary

The suite's selected configurations remain valid and its coverage purpose addresses the relevant change; behavioural oracles are separately checked.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Retain still-valid tests and manually add a few relevant configurations when changes are small.

Support and retirement

Remove tests for unsupported configurations only after support decisions; retain a cheap fresh-generation path when repairing costs more.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Old tests exercise invalid or irrelevant configurations while newly introduced configurations receive no attention. No numerical benefit is asserted.

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The suite's selected configurations remain valid and its coverage purpose addresses the relevant change; behavioural oracles are separately checked.

  • Mutation-score and configuration-distance results are proxies, not deployed fault coverage or measured human repair labour. Higher-order mutations and richer models can change the ranking.

  • Regeneration/repair computation, rebuilding test environments and updating behavioural expectations.

ESPLE-036 — Lifecycle economics with uncertainty

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Product-line economic models compare organisational investment, reusable assets and product construction with alternatives.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S012

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s012

2005-02

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Product-line economic models compare organisational investment, reusable assets and product construction with alternatives.

Problem it addressed:

Reuse savings are celebrated while startup, coordination, assurance, migration and exit costs are omitted.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Reuse savings are celebrated while startup, coordination, assurance, migration and exit costs are omitted.

Mechanism:

Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.

Trigger or context:

An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a coarse scenario comparison when precise estimates are not credible; keep assumptions visible rather than manufacture precision.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Alternative costs, expected products, asset investment, ongoing coordination and support commitments.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.

Variation point and binding time

Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.

Core asset and product relation

Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.

Derivation and configuration identity

Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.

Evolution and migration obligations

Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.

Ownership and product exception policy

Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P8

Property specific application
Family

P8

An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

Consequential inputs

Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.

Acceptance boundary

The decision states the horizon, counterfactual, omitted costs and sensitivity that could reverse the preferred option.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Use a coarse scenario comparison when precise estimates are not credible; keep assumptions visible rather than manufacture precision.

Support and retirement

Replace estimates with actual evidence as available; stop modelling details too small to change the decision.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Reuse savings are celebrated while startup, coordination, assurance, migration and exit costs are omitted. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement.

Actor and authority boundary:

Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Alternative costs, expected products, asset investment, ongoing coordination and support commitments.; the result must expose The decision states the horizon, counterfactual, omitted costs and sensitivity that could reverse the preferred option. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The decision states the horizon, counterfactual, omitted costs and sensitivity that could reverse the preferred option.

Known failure modes:

  • Forecasts may be wrong; reported case benefits are selected and confounded; small task experiments omit transition investment.

  • Estimation, data collection and the risk that elaborate models obscure uncertainty.

ESPLE-038 — Economic reassessment without a sunk-cost veto

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Historical origin:

Formulation

Product-focused scope and lifecycle economic reasoning require ongoing justification, not only a founding business case.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Product-focused scope and lifecycle economic reasoning require ongoing justification, not only a founding business case.

Problem it addressed:

Past investment becomes the reason to retain a costly family structure even after demand or assumptions change.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Past investment becomes the reason to retain a costly family structure even after demand or assumptions change.

Mechanism:

Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.

Trigger or context:

Demand changes, reuse disappoints, coordination dominates or the product portfolio contracts.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A brief decision review using actual product experience may replace a recurrent formal business-case ceremony.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Current support obligations, observed costs and credible future alternatives.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.

Variation point and binding time

Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.

Core asset and product relation

Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.

Derivation and configuration identity

Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.

Evolution and migration obligations

Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.

Ownership and product exception policy

Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

Non family or cheaper alternative

A brief decision review using actual product experience may replace a recurrent formal business-case ceremony.

Support and retirement

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Past investment becomes the reason to retain a costly family structure even after demand or assumptions change. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Portfolio sponsors with product and asset maintainers decide future investment; sunk costs explain history but cannot by themselves justify continuation.

Actor and authority boundary:

Portfolio sponsors with product and asset maintainers decide future investment; sunk costs explain history but cannot by themselves justify continuation. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Current support obligations, observed costs and credible future alternatives.; the result must expose Continued shared production has a current rationale, or a bounded transition away from it preserves necessary commitments. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Continued shared production has a current rationale, or a bounded transition away from it preserves necessary commitments.

Known failure modes:

  • Frequent reassessment can destabilise planning; short-term accounting can destroy valuable but slower-payoff shared capability.

  • Strategic review, transition work and possible loss of future option value.

ESPLE-039 — Authority and arbitration for shared assets

Historical source pointer: /properties/38 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Product-line management addresses ownership and conflicting needs around shared assets and production.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S008

  • ESPLE-S011

  • ESPLE-S013

  • ESPLE-S041

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

2001 publication; commonly cited 2002

Esple-s011

2002-06

Esple-s013

2010

2018 conference; 2021-10-12 arXiv deposit

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Product-line management addresses ownership and conflicting needs around shared assets and production.

Problem it addressed:

Teams can identify a shared problem but nobody can authorise a fix, or one product imposes its priorities on all others.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Teams can identify a shared problem but nobody can authorise a fix, or one product imposes its priorities on all others.

Mechanism:

Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.

Trigger or context:

Shared changes affect products with different priorities or authorities.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A named maintainer and direct product-owner agreement can suffice; a new committee is not a property.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Ownership, affected obligations, cost bearers and an escalation path for unresolved conflict.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing can concern code, specifications or interfaces; those forms create different control and compatibility relationships.

Feature semantics and constraints

Features can encode customer or external constraints, but their legal/security applicability must come from competent external evidence.

Variation point and binding time

Authority to bind or rebind a choice is separate from its representability in a model.

Core asset and product relation

Core assets have maintainers and consumers; externally owned components and autonomous derivatives are not silently internal assets.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product and asset provenance supports accountability without granting ownership over external participants.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

A common core can create common-mode exposure; external compatibility and product-specific obligations remain part of assurance.

Evolution and migration obligations

Independent release schedules, suppliers and support commitments constrain shared changes and retirement.

Ownership and product exception policy

Contribution, variation, exception and release authority must be explicit and proportionate; a committee is not universally required.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination, training and bottlenecks are costs; simpler ownership or ordinary dependency management can be adequate where no family governance is needed.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P9

Property specific application
Family

P9

Trigger

Shared changes affect products with different priorities or authorities.

Consequential inputs

Ownership, affected obligations, cost bearers and an escalation path for unresolved conflict.

Realisation or decision

Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.

Acceptance boundary

A disputed shared change can receive an accountable decision, and affected products learn its consequences.

Non family or cheaper alternative

A named maintainer and direct product-owner agreement can suffice; a new committee is not a property.

Support and retirement

Simplify authority arrangements when the portfolio or conflict surface shrinks; preserve accountability for supported products.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Teams can identify a shared problem but nobody can authorise a fix, or one product imposes its priorities on all others. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Product and core decision-makers exchange impact and priority information; evidence of a technical opportunity is separate from authority to act.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product and core decision-makers exchange impact and priority information; evidence of a technical opportunity is separate from authority to act. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Ownership, affected obligations, cost bearers and an escalation path for unresolved conflict.; the result must expose A disputed shared change can receive an accountable decision, and affected products learn its consequences. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A disputed shared change can receive an accountable decision, and affected products learn its consequences.

Known failure modes:

  • Central ownership can become a queue and incentive bottleneck. Open ecosystems may lack a single authority and require negotiated boundaries instead.

  • Negotiation, delay and the cost of shared priorities that do not maximise every product locally.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Central ownership can become a queue and incentive bottleneck. Open ecosystems may lack a single authority and require negotiated boundaries instead.

Organisational readiness and management are part of product-line adoption rather than consequences of installing tools.

Teams are rewarded for immediate local delivery while expected to invest in shared assets and absorb others' requirements.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Teams are rewarded for immediate local delivery while expected to invest in shared assets and absorb others' requirements.

Mechanism:

Align skills, capacity, incentives and cost allocation with the intended shared-production responsibilities; scale commitments to actual capability.

Trigger or context:

A product-line plan requires work or coordination beyond the existing organisation's supported practice.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Start with a limited shared capability and existing staff rather than create a full platform organisation before demand is known.

Skill gaps, delivery commitments, maintenance capacity and how shared costs and benefits are distributed.

Family scope and expected reuse

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Evolution and migration obligations

Contribution, variation, exception and release authority must be explicit and proportionate; a committee is not universally required.

ESPLE-041 — An explicit ecosystem participation boundary

Historical source pointer: /properties/40 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Ecosystem work expands variability concerns beyond one organisation; community-driven variability may coordinate specifications without a shared implementation core.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S029

  • ESPLE-S044

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s029

2009

Esple-s044

2026-03-21

Lineage class:

DOCUMENTED_EXTERNAL_RELATION

Original form:

Ecosystem work expands variability concerns beyond one organisation; community-driven variability may coordinate specifications without a shared implementation core.

Problem it addressed:

A family model assumes control over external contributors or treats every interoperating derivative as a centrally derived product.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A family model assumes control over external contributors or treats every interoperating derivative as a centrally derived product.

Mechanism:

Identify who controls assets, proposals, interfaces and releases; distinguish contractual or negotiated compatibility from internal derivation authority; export bounded interfaces rather than fictitious central control.

Trigger or context:

Suppliers, open-source participants or independent platform users determine material variation.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Manage a bounded component dependency when no broader ecosystem coordination is required.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Participant autonomy, shared interface/specification obligations and actual contribution or compatibility mechanisms.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing can concern code, specifications or interfaces; those forms create different control and compatibility relationships.

Feature semantics and constraints

Features can encode customer or external constraints, but their legal/security applicability must come from competent external evidence.

Variation point and binding time

Authority to bind or rebind a choice is separate from its representability in a model.

Core asset and product relation

Core assets have maintainers and consumers; externally owned components and autonomous derivatives are not silently internal assets.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product and asset provenance supports accountability without granting ownership over external participants.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

A common core can create common-mode exposure; external compatibility and product-specific obligations remain part of assurance.

Evolution and migration obligations

Independent release schedules, suppliers and support commitments constrain shared changes and retirement.

Ownership and product exception policy

Contribution, variation, exception and release authority must be explicit and proportionate; a committee is not universally required.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination, training and bottlenecks are costs; simpler ownership or ordinary dependency management can be adequate where no family governance is needed.

Profile id

Family

Acceptance boundary

Shared claims identify their organisational reach; independent products are not silently counted as conforming family instances.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Manage a bounded component dependency when no broader ecosystem coordination is required.

Support and retirement

Omit ecosystem machinery when the relevant relationship is only ordinary dependency consumption.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A family model assumes control over external contributors or treats every interoperating derivative as a centrally derived product. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Platform maintainers and external participants negotiate evidence and compatibility; one organisation cannot unilaterally authorise changes to autonomous derivatives.

Actor and authority boundary:

Platform maintainers and external participants negotiate evidence and compatibility; one organisation cannot unilaterally authorise changes to autonomous derivatives. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Participant autonomy, shared interface/specification obligations and actual contribution or compatibility mechanisms.; the result must expose Shared claims identify their organisational reach; independent products are not silently counted as conforming family instances. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Shared claims identify their organisational reach; independent products are not silently counted as conforming family instances.

Known failure modes:

  • Ecosystem taxonomy does not prove effective governance or economic superiority. Central product-line controls can be both infeasible and inappropriate in autonomous communities.

  • Negotiation, compatibility testing and incomplete knowledge of independently evolving implementations.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Ecosystem taxonomy does not prove effective governance or economic superiority. Central product-line controls can be both infeasible and inappropriate in autonomous communities.

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Formulation

Dynamic product lines combine runtime context observation with constrained selection and reconfiguration of features.

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s030

2008

Esple-s031

2023

Esple-s043

2008

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Dynamic product lines combine runtime context observation with constrained selection and reconfiguration of features.

Problem it addressed:

Runtime adaptation is improvised without a known family of admissible alternatives or a relation between context and capability.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Runtime adaptation is improvised without a known family of admissible alternatives or a relation between context and capability.

Mechanism:

Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.

Trigger or context:

A product must change its selected capabilities during execution as conditions change.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Select a static or deployment-time variant when runtime rebinding is not required.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Observable context, supported configurations, adaptation goals and a feasible reconfiguration mechanism.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.

Feature semantics and constraints

Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.

Variation point and binding time

Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.

Core asset and product relation

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Derivation and configuration identity

Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P10

Property specific application
Family

P10

Trigger

A product must change its selected capabilities during execution as conditions change.

Consequential inputs

Observable context, supported configurations, adaptation goals and a feasible reconfiguration mechanism.

Realisation or decision

Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.

Acceptance boundary

A context change leads to a permitted, realised configuration or a diagnosed inability to reconfigure; actual state is observed afterwards.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Select a static or deployment-time variant when runtime rebinding is not required.

Support and retirement

Eliminate dynamic control when operating conditions no longer require runtime product variation.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Runtime adaptation is improvised without a known family of admissible alternatives or a relation between context and capability. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Operators and adaptation designers define the allowed policy; a runtime controller acts only within the authority and capabilities supplied to it.

Actor and authority boundary:

Operators and adaptation designers define the allowed policy; a runtime controller acts only within the authority and capabilities supplied to it. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Observable context, supported configurations, adaptation goals and a feasible reconfiguration mechanism.; the result must expose A context change leads to a permitted, realised configuration or a diagnosed inability to reconfigure; actual state is observed afterwards. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A context change leads to a permitted, realised configuration or a diagnosed inability to reconfigure; actual state is observed afterwards.

Known failure modes:

  • Sensors can be stale, context models incomplete and adaptation goals conflicting. Arbitrary adaptation does not become a DSPL merely by being dynamic.

  • Monitoring, runtime state, actuation and additional assurance of transitions.

Important criticisms:

Property specific objection

Sensors can be stale, context models incomplete and adaptation goals conflicting. Arbitrary adaptation does not become a DSPL merely by being dynamic.

Original form:

Dynamic variability introduces transition requirements in addition to endpoint configuration validity.

Two individually acceptable configurations can be connected only through an unsafe intermediate state or loss of operational state.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Two individually acceptable configurations can be connected only through an unsafe intermediate state or loss of operational state.

Mechanism:

Check the transition path, quiescence or state transfer and actual controllability; preserve safety requirements throughout the operating phase or enter a separately justified safe reconfiguration phase.

Features or components are rebound while the system is operating.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Stop and restart in a known safe condition, or prohibit runtime switching, when live transition assurance is disproportionate.

Current state, intermediate-state constraints, controllable actions, timing assumptions and recovery behaviour.

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Original form:

Supervisory control is imported into dynamic feature configuration using discrete-event models and controllable/uncontrollable events.

Problem it addressed:

A runtime controller may allow requirement-violating behaviour or block necessary completion when features change.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A runtime controller may allow requirement-violating behaviour or block necessary completion when features change.

Mechanism:

Synthesize a supervisor for the modelled plant and requirements, then establish that observations, event controllability and actuation match the implementation.

Trigger or context:

A finite-state or otherwise supported discrete-event model adequately captures a consequential dynamic product-line problem.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A reviewed transition table or offline configuration can suffice where synthesis adds no justified assurance.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Plant model, marked states, requirements, event partition and a faithful implementation mapping.

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

Within the model, the supervisor is safe, controllable and nonblocking as specified; implementation checks support transfer of the relevant result.

Known failure modes:

  • Nonblocking permits reachability of a marked state, not inevitable progress on every run. Industrial-origin benchmark success does not certify a deployed physical system.

  • Modelling, synthesis, state-space management and model/plant validation.

Nonblocking permits reachability of a marked state, not inevitable progress on every run. Industrial-origin benchmark success does not certify a deployed physical system.

Supervisory control is imported into dynamic feature configuration using discrete-event models and controllable/uncontrollable events.

Criticism and change

Nonblocking permits reachability of a marked state, not inevitable progress on every run. Industrial-origin benchmark success does not certify a deployed physical system. Mature response: Synthesize a supervisor for the modelled plant and requirements, then establish that observations, event controllability and actuation match the implementation.

ESPLE-046 — Semantic fidelity in variability interchange

Historical source pointer: /properties/45 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Formulation

UVL addresses feature-model interchange through defined language levels; standards and tools have distinct scopes.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S032

  • ESPLE-S033

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s032

2025

Esple-s033

2021-04

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

UVL addresses feature-model interchange through defined language levels; standards and tools have distinct scopes.

Problem it addressed:

A model parses in another tool but loses constraints, value semantics or configuration meaning.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A model parses in another tool but loses constraints, value semantics or configuration meaning.

Mechanism:

Specify the supported language level and check semantic preservation for translations and toolchains; make unsupported constructs explicit.

Trigger or context:

Variability models move across tools, organisations or analysis backends.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Keep one stable representation and tool when interchange has no real consumer.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Source and destination semantics, supported versions and a meaningful equivalence or conformance test.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.

Feature semantics and constraints

Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.

Variation point and binding time

Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.

Core asset and product relation

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Derivation and configuration identity

Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P10
