Support and retirement

Remove conversions whose consumer disappears; preserve native evidence rather than flatten richer semantics silently.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A model parses in another tool but loses constraints, value semantics or configuration meaning. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Tool integrators and model consumers agree the interchange contract; a shared extension does not automatically become a normative standard.

Actor and authority boundary:

Tool integrators and model consumers agree the interchange contract; a shared extension does not automatically become a normative standard. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Source and destination semantics, supported versions and a meaningful equivalence or conformance test.; the result must expose Relevant configurations and constraints survive interchange, or the loss is detected before relying on the result. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Relevant configurations and constraints survive interchange, or the loss is detected before relying on the result.

Known failure modes:

  • A common syntax is not universal semantic compatibility, and community adoption does not establish economic benefit.

  • Conversion testing, compatibility maintenance and handling unsupported language features.

Property specific objection

A common syntax is not universal semantic compatibility, and community adoption does not establish economic benefit.

ESPLE-048 — LLM regeneration as a superior replacement for maintained variability

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Formulation

A June 2026 exploratory proposal suggests producing variants by LLM regeneration from specifications rather than maintaining conventional variability structures.

  • ESPLE-S034

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s034

2026-06-17

Lineage class:

HYBRIDISATION

Original form:

A June 2026 exploratory proposal suggests producing variants by LLM regeneration from specifications rather than maintaining conventional variability structures.

Problem it addressed:

Conventional variability can be costly to maintain, but regeneration may lose provenance, consistency and accumulated assurance.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Conventional variability can be costly to maintain, but regeneration may lose provenance, consistency and accumulated assurance.

Mechanism:

The candidate is a replacement strategy: retain specifications and regenerate variants. Its stronger claim of superior lifecycle adequacy is not established by the inspected evidence.

Trigger or context:

Considering regeneration as a substitute for a maintained family realisation, not merely as assistance.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Keep maintained assets and use an assistant only for bounded changes; conventional generation remains an alternative.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Stable specifications, independently checked outputs, versioned models/tooling and longitudinal cost/defect evidence.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.

Feature semantics and constraints

Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.

Variation point and binding time

Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.

Core asset and product relation

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Derivation and configuration identity

Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

ESPLE-049 — A universal break-even product count

Historical source pointer: /properties/48 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Adversarial universalisation of illustrative break-even claims; not attributed to all product-line researchers.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S012

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s012

2005-02

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial universalisation of illustrative break-even claims; not attributed to all product-line researchers.

Problem it addressed:

A fixed product count is substituted for a context-specific investment comparison.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A fixed product count is substituted for a context-specific investment comparison.

Mechanism:

No general mechanism supports the universal threshold. Replace the claim with a horizon-specific comparison of investment, derivation, coordination and support costs.

Trigger or context:

A proposed adoption is justified by reaching a supposedly universal number of products.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A small scenario calculation showing the relevant cost drivers is adequate to reject the fixed threshold.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Actual cost structure, demand uncertainty and a credible non-product-line baseline.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.

Variation point and binding time

Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.

Core asset and product relation

Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.

Derivation and configuration identity

Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.

Evolution and migration obligations

Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.

Ownership and product exception policy

Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

ESPLE-050 — A complete upfront platform as a prerequisite

Historical source pointer: /properties/49 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Adversarial reading of proactive domain engineering as a compulsory complete upfront platform.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S010

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s010

2001 workshop; 2002 proceedings

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial reading of proactive domain engineering as a compulsory complete upfront platform.

Problem it addressed:

Adoption is blocked or over-invested because every possible variation is demanded before any product experience.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Adoption is blocked or over-invested because every possible variation is demanded before any product experience.

Mechanism:

Reject the universal prerequisite; use the proactive, reactive, extractive or hybrid route justified by the actual starting conditions.

Trigger or context:

A process requires complete domain assets before permitting useful product work.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Start with a bounded common asset and one product, then expand only when evidence warrants it.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Current assets, product urgency and uncertainty about future variation.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.

Commonality and variability assumptions

The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.

Feature semantics and constraints

Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.

Variation point and binding time

Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.

Core asset and product relation

Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.

Evolution and migration obligations

Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.

Ownership and product exception policy

The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

Acceptance boundary

Upfront work is limited to what the chosen route and product obligations actually require.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Start with a bounded common asset and one product, then expand only when evidence warrants it.

Support and retirement

Remove the compulsory rule; retain bounded proactive investment where it earns its cost.

Actor and authority boundary:

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Upfront work is limited to what the chosen route and product obligations actually require.

ESPLE-051 — A feature-tree artefact as sufficient variability management

Historical source pointer: /properties/50 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Feature-tree-only observance is a caricature: original FODA included more than a diagram.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S005

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s005

1990-11

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Feature-tree-only observance is a caricature: original FODA included more than a diagram.

Problem it addressed:

The presence of a model artefact is treated as proof of managed variability.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

The presence of a model artefact is treated as proof of managed variability.

Mechanism:

Reject artefact sufficiency; require meaningful features, usable constraints, a relation to realisation and an actual configuration or change consumer.

Trigger or context:

A diagram, modelling tool or documentation checklist is offered as the evidence of control.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A checked decision table or direct configuration rules may supply the required function without a tree.

Dependencies or preconditions:

The decision the artefact supports and evidence that it remains aligned with products.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common and variable characteristics are explicit semantic decisions; historical product observations do not exhaust valid possibilities.

Feature semantics and constraints

Boolean, cardinality, attribute and typed constraints describe encoded validity; domain adequacy must be checked outside solver consistency.

Variation point and binding time

A model choice may bind before build, at deployment or at runtime; selection semantics do not determine realisation timing by themselves.

Core asset and product relation

Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.

Derivation and configuration identity

A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.

Ownership and product exception policy

Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial promotion of model satisfiability into a guarantee about delivered implementation behaviour.

Problem it addressed:

Omitted constraints or a defective generator produce incorrect products from an encoded-valid configuration.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Omitted constraints or a defective generator produce incorrect products from an encoded-valid configuration.

Mechanism:

Reject the implication. Keep model consistency, realisation correctness and product behaviour as separate claims with explicit connecting premises.

Trigger or context:

A SAT result is used to assert product correctness or release readiness.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Show a concrete missing domain constraint or faulty realisation to expose the gap; retain the SAT check for its genuine purpose.

Dependencies or preconditions:

The actual encoded formula, generator/implementation relation and product obligations.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.

Feature semantics and constraints

Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.

Variation point and binding time

Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.

Core asset and product relation

Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.

Derivation and configuration identity

Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.

Ownership and product exception policy

Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

ESPLE-054 — Later binding as universally better

Historical source pointer: /properties/53 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Adversarial ranking that treats later binding as always more mature because it preserves choice.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S030

  • ESPLE-S042

  • ESPLE-S043

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s030

2008

Esple-s042

2005

Esple-s043

2008

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial ranking that treats later binding as always more mature because it preserves choice.

Problem it addressed:

Unneeded runtime variation introduces retained code, state and transition hazards.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Unneeded runtime variation introduces retained code, state and transition hazards.

Mechanism:

Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.

Trigger or context:

A compile/deployment-time choice is moved later without a concrete operational need.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Fix the choice earlier and rebuild or redeploy when rare changes occur.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Change frequency, latency requirements, footprint and transition obligations.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Shared code, product-specific code and interaction glue may coexist; arbitrary duplication is neither automatically valuable nor forbidden.

Feature semantics and constraints

Selection-to-implementation relations must preserve feature meaning; syntactic modularity alone does not establish semantic alignment.

Variation point and binding time

Compile, deployment and runtime binding carry different footprint, timing and transition obligations; later is not universally better.

Core asset and product relation

Assets may be annotated, composed, parameterised or transformed; the core need not be one monolithic source tree.

Derivation and configuration identity

Generator, template, build and dependency versions can affect the realised variant and belong in relevant provenance.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Cross-mechanism interactions require checks; successful code generation or compilation is not product correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Changes to realisation or binding time can invalidate mappings, supported configurations and previous assurance.

Ownership and product exception policy

Implementers choose within family obligations; product-local exceptions require explicit support and do not inherit all shared claims.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Technique complexity must be earned by demand and assurance needs; ordinary parameters, modules or manual derivation remain alternatives.

ESPLE-DP-P4

Architects and operators assess the actual need for late choice; flexibility is not an end in itself.

Actor and authority boundary:

Architects and operators assess the actual need for late choice; flexibility is not an end in itself. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

Each late-bound choice has a justified consumer and an assurance path for its extra reachable states.

Known failure modes:

  • Earlier binding can be unacceptable when context changes faster than redeployment; the ranking fails in both directions.

  • Runtime machinery and verification versus extra builds and reduced responsiveness.

A small well-managed family is rejected as not a product line because some derivation choices remain manual.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A small well-managed family is rejected as not a product line because some derivation choices remain manual.

Mechanism:

Reject total automation as a universal definition; require a defined, adequate derivation method and evidence for the resulting products.

Trigger or context:

Automation percentage is used as the criterion for product-line existence or maturity.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A reliable reviewed manual derivation can be sufficient for a small stable family.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Product volume, error consequences, required repeatability and a real production plan.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.

Feature semantics and constraints

A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.

Variation point and binding time

Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.

Core asset and product relation

Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.

Derivation and configuration identity

Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.

Evolution and migration obligations

Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.

Ownership and product exception policy

Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

ESPLE-DP-P5

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A small well-managed family is rejected as not a product line because some derivation choices remain manual. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Product builders and managers judge production adequacy; narrower standard or method definitions must be named rather than universalised.

Actor and authority boundary:

Product builders and managers judge production adequacy; narrower standard or method definitions must be named rather than universalised. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

The consequential exchange is the following input and result, between the consumer roles already identified: Product volume, error consequences, required repeatability and a real production plan.; the result must expose The family can reliably derive supported products, with consequential manual decisions explicit and checked. No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

The family can reliably derive supported products, with consequential manual decisions explicit and checked.

Known failure modes:

  • Manual derivation can become error-prone or too slow at scale; some specialised approaches do require stronger automation within their stated scope.

  • Full automation can exceed its benefit; insufficient automation can create repeated labour and mistakes.

Property specific objection

Manual derivation can become error-prone or too slow at scale; some specialised approaches do require stronger automation within their stated scope.

ESPLE-057 — Clone-and-own as universally inadmissible

Historical source pointer: /properties/56 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Adversarial moralisation of clone-and-own as always inferior to managed shared production.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S026

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s026

2013

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial moralisation of clone-and-own as always inferior to managed shared production.

Problem it addressed:

Product autonomy, startup speed or low expected reuse are ignored in selecting an engineering strategy.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Product autonomy, startup speed or low expected reuse are ignored in selecting an engineering strategy.

Mechanism:

Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.

Trigger or context:

Cloning is rejected without examining portfolio conditions or maintenance obligations.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Retain clones with sufficient provenance and targeted shared-fix tracking when they are the lower-cost adequate solution.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Product divergence, expected common changes, ownership constraints and a realistic lifecycle horizon.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.

Variation point and binding time

Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.

Core asset and product relation

Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.

Derivation and configuration identity

Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.

Evolution and migration obligations

Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.

Ownership and product exception policy

Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

ESPLE-058 — Stable names or configuration sets as behavioural compatibility

Historical source pointer: /properties/57 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Analytical counter-proposition examined against the cited tradition; not attributed as a consensus belief.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Adversarial equivalence between stable feature names or permitted sets and preservation of product behaviour.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S023

  • ESPLE-S024

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s023

2009

Esple-s024

2013 preprint/online; 2014 journal

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial equivalence between stable feature names or permitted sets and preservation of product behaviour.

Problem it addressed:

The same selection yields changed behaviour after a core, generator or semantic update.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

The same selection yields changed behaviour after a core, generator or semantic update.

Mechanism:

Reject the equivalence; preserve or explicitly change feature intent and verify the actual migrated product's obligations.

Trigger or context:

Compatibility is asserted solely because names or model-level product sets did not change.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A targeted behavioural regression can be sufficient where a full migration analysis adds nothing.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Old/new feature meanings, realisation versions and relevant behavioural expectations.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Model and product maintainers communicate semantic change; model equivalence does not authorise silent behavioural changes. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Observable postcondition:

Compatibility claims name what is preserved and are supported at that level.

Known failure modes:

  • Model-set equivalence remains valuable for its own purpose; it is not disproved by an implementation change outside the model.

  • False compatibility can break supported products; appropriate checking adds regression and communication effort.

Model-set equivalence remains valuable for its own purpose; it is not disproved by an implementation change outside the model.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Configuration counting is a legitimate analysis operation, but maximising that count is not an established engineering objective.

Problem it addressed:

A larger theoretical product space is presented as benefit despite unused options and greater assurance burden.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

A larger theoretical product space is presented as benefit despite unused options and greater assurance burden.

Mechanism:

Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.

Trigger or context:

Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Count supported or demanded products and their costs when theoretical possibilities do not affect the decision.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Validity constraints, demand evidence and the purpose of the metric.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.

Variation point and binding time

Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.

Core asset and product relation

Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.

Derivation and configuration identity

Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.

Evolution and migration obligations

Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.

Ownership and product exception policy

Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

Profile id

P8

Support and retirement

Stop reporting the count when it has no decision consumer; retain it when needed to plan coverage or support.

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: A larger theoretical product space is presented as benefit despite unused options and greater assurance burden. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Portfolio and assurance planners interpret the count; a metric collector cannot infer market value from arithmetic.

Actor and authority boundary:

Portfolio and assurance planners interpret the count; a metric collector cannot infer market value from arithmetic. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.

Communication or interaction requirement:

No separate meeting, team or owner is required merely by this record.

Observable postcondition:

A reported count is tied to a concrete planning use and is not equated with realised benefit.

Known failure modes:

  • Counts can be inflated by irrelevant options or inconsistent feature granularity; large spaces may nonetheless matter for assurance planning.

  • Gaming encourages unnecessary variability; counting rich models may itself be expensive.

Counts can be inflated by irrelevant options or inconsistent feature granularity; large spaces may nonetheless matter for assurance planning.

ESPLE-060 — Formal modelling as operational authority

Historical source pointer: /properties/59 in the exact public ledger.

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Formulation

Adversarial conflation of a modelled controllable event with authority and practical ability to perform the real action.

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Adversarial conflation of a modelled controllable event with authority and practical ability to perform the real action.

Problem it addressed:

An adaptation design assumes it may change components, users' choices or physical actuators merely because the model allows it.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

An adaptation design assumes it may change components, users' choices or physical actuators merely because the model allows it.

Mechanism:

Reject self-authorising control; separately establish observation, actual actuation capability, external permission and the expected consequence.

Trigger or context:

A formal or generated controller is proposed for real runtime configuration.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Keep the result advisory or use an existing authorised operational process when actuation is not established.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Model/plant mapping, permissions, controllability and operational feedback.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.

Feature semantics and constraints

Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.

Variation point and binding time

Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.

Core asset and product relation

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Derivation and configuration identity

Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

ESPLE-061 — Support-aware retirement of variability

Historical source pointer: /properties/60 in the exact public ledger.

Lineage id:

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Candidate origin:

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

Industrial legacy management can exclude old variation from new products while retaining artefacts needed for supported products.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S007

  • ESPLE-S011

  • ESPLE-S041

  • ESPLE-S045

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s007

1999

Esple-s011

2002-06

Esple-s041

2018 conference; 2021-10-12 arXiv deposit

Esple-s045

2026-04-17

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

Industrial legacy management can exclude old variation from new products while retaining artefacts needed for supported products.

Problem it addressed:

Obsolete options burden new derivation, but indiscriminate removal destroys the ability to maintain older variants.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Obsolete options burden new derivation, but indiscriminate removal destroys the ability to maintain older variants.

Mechanism:

Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.

Trigger or context:

A feature is unused for new demand, fixed to one value or becomes disproportionately costly to support.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Mark the feature unavailable to new configurations while retaining the older baseline, rather than immediately rewriting all code.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Actual usage, supported products, external commitments and the effect of removal on derivation and tests.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.

Feature semantics and constraints

Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.

Variation point and binding time

Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.

Core asset and product relation

Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.

Derivation and configuration identity

Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.

Ownership and product exception policy

Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

Profile id

ESPLE-DP-P7

Property specific application
Family

P7

Trigger

A feature is unused for new demand, fixed to one value or becomes disproportionately costly to support.

Consequential inputs

Actual usage, supported products, external commitments and the effect of removal on derivation and tests.

Realisation or decision

Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.

Acceptance boundary

New products no longer inherit unnecessary variation, and supported older products retain an adequate maintenance or migration path.

Non family or cheaper alternative

Mark the feature unavailable to new configurations while retaining the older baseline, rather than immediately rewriting all code.

Support and retirement

End the retirement control itself when no supported product or retained obligation depends on the old variation.

Expected engineering payoff:

Avoid or reveal this failure without imposing the fuller mechanism where unnecessary: Obsolete options burden new derivation, but indiscriminate removal destroys the ability to maintain older variants. No numerical benefit is asserted.

Decision or consumer:

Actor and authority boundary:

ESPLE-062 — Null configurability as context-independent behaviour

Historical source pointer: /properties/61 in the exact public ledger.

EVOLVED_SOFTWARE_PRODUCT_LINE_ENGINEERING

Source-grounded mechanism or claim registered during this independent study; no target or sibling vocabulary supplied the candidate.

Historical origin:

Formulation

A 2026 null-variability proposal combines early binding with broad behavioural-consistency wording, while also allowing non-identical outputs for different inputs.

Source ids

  • ESPLE-S045

Dating rule

Dates identify inspected formulations, not proof that the earliest listed work invented every element.

Source dates
Esple-s045

2026-04-17

Lineage class:

WITHIN_TRADITION_ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION

Original form:

A 2026 null-variability proposal combines early binding with broad behavioural-consistency wording, while also allowing non-identical outputs for different inputs.

Problem it addressed:

Absence of configuration choices is interpreted as proof that execution is independent of environment or always predictable.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Absence of configuration choices is interpreted as proof that execution is independent of environment or always predictable.

Mechanism:

Reject that stronger implication. Retain the narrower distinction that selected features are fixed after a declared binding time; analyse inputs, state, timing and environment separately.

Trigger or context:

Fixed feature selection is used to infer environment-independent behaviour or a general correctness guarantee.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A fixed-function program that reads a changing external value supplies a logical counterexample to the stronger inference.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A clear separation of configuration, ordinary input, internal state and operating environment.

Domain profile:

Family scope and expected reuse

Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.

Commonality and variability assumptions

A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.

Feature semantics and constraints

Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.

Variation point and binding time

Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.

Core asset and product relation

Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.

Derivation and configuration identity

Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.

Feature interaction and coverage boundary

Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.

Evolution and migration obligations

Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.

Ownership and product exception policy

Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.

Economic assumptions and non product line alternative

Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.
